newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo sees pulp price under pressure now.
newsitem.headline: MoDo sees pulp price under pressure now.

text.p: Swedish forestry company MoDo said pulp prices were currently under pressure, and that hedging operations contributed a substantial 1.37 billion crowns to its nine-month profit.
MoDo said its profit after financial items in the period to September 30 fell 43 percent to 2.47 billion crowns ($372 million) on a year earlier.
The figure was a touch higher than an average market forecast that it would make a 2.24 billion crown profit.
The nine-month profit was achieved on lower sales of 15.0 billion crowns ($2.3 billion) against 17.26 billion a year earlier, and MoDo said lower prices and deliveries were behind the fall.
The last major Swedish forestry group to announce nine-month results, MoDo said demand for its products had steadily improved and that deliveries picked up in the third quarter.
"This is attributable partly to the stock situation in the client and distribution chain returning to normal after a long period of stock reduction," it said.
Price increases went through for pulp, fine paper and wood products. "At the moment, there is meanwhile a certain pressure of price on pulp," the company said in a statement.
MoDo's profit per share halved to 18.80 crowns from 36.10
The group produced 1,998,000 tonnes of paper, cartons and pulp for external customers in the nine months, 189,000 tonnes less than for the corresponding period of 1995.
Deliveries of paper, cartons and pulp in the period were 2,014,000 tonnes compared with 2,107,000, but deliveries picked up by two percent in the third quarter to 710,000 tonnes.
MoDo's share price rose on the result and at 1120 GMT was 7.5 crowns higher at 185 crowns.
